name: Passbolt
summary: Passbolt is an open-source password manager built for teams, which can run it on their own servers or use Passbolt's cloud hosted in Europe. The self-hosted Community Edition is free for any number of users, and paid plans start at $4.90 per user a month with a 10-user minimum.

facts.text: Passbolt's code, including the paid Pro edition, is open source under the AGPLv3 license.
Encryption is based on OpenPGP, and each user's secret key is never sent to the server in cleartext.
Passbolt publishes third-party audit reports, including Cure53 audits from 2021 to 2026 and a Quarkslab evaluation of Pro version 5.4.
Passbolt's SOC 2 Type II audit was carried out by Johanson Group, and customers can request the report under a non-disclosure agreement.

On October 29, 2026, Passbolt released fixes in Pro version 5.17 for a high-severity server-side request forgery issue and a weakness in its limit on repeated MFA attempts, and advised all administrators to update.
Passbolt keeps a public list of past vulnerabilities and outages going back to 2017.

plans.name: Community Edition
plans.notes: Self-hosted. No single sign-on, LDAP, activity log or password policies.

plans.name: Cloud Business
plans.notes: Hosted by Passbolt in Belgium and Germany. Billed annually; $5.40 billed monthly. Minimum 10 users.

plans.name: Cloud Sovereign
plans.notes: Hosted in a private data center in Luxembourg. Billed annually. Minimum 10 users.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Self-hosted or cloud, with a 4-hour support response time

hiddenCosts: Pro, Cloud Business and Cloud Sovereign require at least 10 users.
LDAP and Active Directory provisioning are not part of Cloud Business.
Cloud annual plans are bought in user tiers; going over the paid count is invoiced at the next tier straight away, and the count does not shrink by itself.
Self-hosted editions run on servers you provide and maintain.

contract.cancellation: Cloud customers can end the service with notice; prepaid fees are not refunded for a termination of convenience.
contract.dataExport: An encrypted KeePass (KDBX) file. Plain CSV export has been off by default since version 5.10 and an administrator can turn it on in the server settings.
